status: bounded systematic scoping review; not exhaustive

sources.title: Construyendo la verdad: minería de texto y redes lingüísticas en audiencias públicas del Caso 03 de la JEP
sources.inspected: §3 pp9–10; regional/role network results; 44-page primary PDF
sources.data: 441 official Case03 videos through 2025-02-02; Spanish auto-subtitles; six subcases including Casanare; selective audio/manual quality control
sources.method: Sentiment and skip-gram/co-occurrence networks, modularity and centrality; descriptive regional/speaker comparisons
sources.result: Existing direct JEP text-mining and linguistic-network study; not expert conditional harm/reparation retrieval.
sources.limits: Excludes unsubtitled videos; selective rather than exhaustive audio checking; lexical communities do not validate moral relevance.
sources.gap: Closest direct JEP counterexample. Novelty must concern validated conditional relevance and source fidelity, not JEP NLP or visualizations.

sources.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
sources.inspected: PDF pp3–9, §§3–4, expert-validation design; later results not independently inspected
sources.data: 1042 items: 305 MCQ,682 semi-open,55 open; ten Colombian legal areas; five workshops
sources.method: Legal-assistant review, specialized evaluator and committee; MCQ accuracy; free-text reference metrics and RAG evaluation
sources.limits: Three specialist evaluators; mostly one per area; no formal independent double-coding/IAA; legal QA differs from testimony relevance.
sources.gap: Do not claim absence of Colombian legal benchmarks; require explicit specialist disagreement and source-grounded harm-response ranking.

sources.title: MEL: Legal Spanish language model
sources.data: Spanish legal corpus; 5.52 million 512-token chunks; MultiEURLEX and private legal classification evaluation
sources.method: XLM-R-large continued masked language modeling; classification comparisons
sources.result: Reports improved classification learning/performance over base models.
sources.limits: Spain/EU formal law; no inspected victim-testimony similarity or moral-conditional ranking evaluation. HTML date metadata conflicts with arXivv1 year.
sources.gap: Legal-language adaptation is established; test actual Colombian oral testimony transfer instead of assuming it.

sources.title: MultiLegalPile: A 689GB Multilingual Legal Corpus
sources.data: 24 languages,17 jurisdictions; native legal corpora, Eurlex and legal-filtered mC4
sources.method: Multilingual and monolingual masked-language-model adaptation; LEXTREME/LexGLUE evaluation
sources.result: Multilingual legal encoders and many improved monolingual legal models already exist.
sources.limits: mC4 precision inspection has small language-specific samples; legal benchmark aggregate does not establish Colombian victim-cultural understanding.
sources.gap: Use available multilingual/legal models as comparators; distinguish legal register, language and normative condition.

sources.title: Spanish Legalese Language Model and Corpora
sources.data: 8.9GB Spanish legal corpus; general Spanish POS,NER,STS,classification,paraphrase,NLI tests
sources.result: Legal embeddings predate this project; Table2 does not show superiority to general Spanish RoBERTa.
sources.limits: Fixed model hyperparameters versus searched comparator; no domain-specific evaluation then available.
sources.gap: Do not presume legal pretraining improves semantic similarity; include an empirical baseline rather than novelty claim.

sources.title: BLEnD: A Benchmark for LLMs on Everyday Knowledge in Diverse Cultures and Languages
sources.data: 16 countries/regions,13 languages; Spain/Mexico Spanish; 500 templates across six everyday categories; native annotators
sources.method: Short-answer and multiple-choice cultural knowledge; typically five valid responses; native local review
sources.result: Cultural/language performance disparities; Spanish is not one cultural unit.
sources.limits: No Colombia in Table1; everyday practices differ from contested moral judgments; national categories miss within-group variation.
sources.gap: Collect plural local relevance judgments, not a single Spanish-cultural gold label.

sources.title: MET / MET-D and MCLASH
sources.data: Culturally adapted CLASH across English,Chinese,Hindi,Korean,Malay,Spanish; 1852 situations and9260 character descriptions
sources.method: 37 grounds in six dimensions; instance-specific ground selection then reasoning; synthetic character-priority rejection/self-distillation
sources.result: Authors report multilingual moral-decision improvements; this is a direct theory-conditioning/training predecessor.
sources.limits: Language used as cultural proxy; character-priority synthetic labels are not Colombian victim judgments; no evidence here of validated harm-reparation geometry.
sources.gap: Theory prompting and multilingual moral distillation cannot be novel claims. Test whether local collective-harm semantics survive conditioning.

sources.title: Legal-ES: A Set of Large Scale Resources for Spanish Legal Text Processing
sources.data: Spanish public legal sources, principally Spain/Europe/international with Mexico/Argentina resource leads; availability-driven sampling
sources.method: 300-dimensional raw/lemmatized embeddings, BOE topic models and preliminary document community graphs
sources.result: Legal semantic navigation and community visualization are established.
sources.limits: Qualitative neighbors/topics; graph experiments explicitly preliminary; planned NER annotation is not completed conditional-relevance gold.
sources.gap: Do not repackage legal similarity graphs as novel; demonstrate held-out validated retrieval utility.

sources.title: JEP abre Caso09 para investigar crímenes contra pueblos y territorios étnicos
sources.inspected: Communiqué075,2022-09-13, substantive paragraphs on territory and intergenerational practices
sources.data: Institutional description; not a labeled dataset
sources.method: Official normative/contextual authority, not an NLP experiment
sources.result: Collective and territorial victim subjects, sacred/spiritual relations, knowledge transmission and intergenerational effects are central.
sources.limits: Does not authorize a universal harm ontology or substitute for community-specific validation.
sources.gap: Individual-utility-only relevance can omit legally/contextually material harm.
